text:
The closest match to the farm's future climate is Garfield County, Washington, which has a good match quality, meaning its climate today is 1.09 sigma away from the future climate. Five out of eight climate models agree on this match. Lower sigma means the place's climate today is closer to the farm's future climate. 

Four matching areas use the field's current rotation of Winter wheat to Fallow. Other rotations used at the matching places include Winter wheat to Spring wheat to Fallow, a flexible mix of fallow and winter wheat, and Winter wheat to Winter wheat to Fallow. 

Compared to the best match, the field today has 37 days above 32 degrees Celsius per year while the match has 42, 165 frost-free days compared to 197 at the match, and its driest-month soil water in September is 16.9 percent compared to 21.3 percent at the match. The afternoon ground temperature in June is 37.9 degrees Celsius here and 39.8 at the match, while in July and August it is 45.6 degrees Celsius here and 46.6 at the match.

By the 2050s under high emissions, temperatures and precipitation will shift across the year. The climate model projections are based on candidate data covering 3351 farmland cells.
